deals.evidence: The $470 million renovation project will maintain a best-in-class NFL stadium
deals.headline: Bengals and Hamilton County finalise Paycor Stadium lease and $470m renovation
deals.summary: New lease keeps the Bengals at Paycor Stadium through June 2036 with options to 2046; a $470m renovation, of which the Bengals invest $120m. Forbes states the county contributes $350m and Ohio committed $600m of infrastructure funding.

stadium_owner.detail: Leased from Hamilton County (lease through June 2036, options to 2046)
stadium_owner.evidence: The Cincinnati Bengals and Hamilton County finalized a new lease that keeps the team in Cincinnati playing home games at Paycor Stadium through June 2036

wages.source_name: Forbes (estimate), player expenses incl. benefits and bonuses

founded_evidence: Planning for the Cincinnati Bengals franchise began three full years before the team began playing in the American Football League in 1968.
name: Cincinnati Bengals
notes: Revenue, operating income, player costs and value are Forbes estimates (2025 season; value calculated September 2026). Founded year is the first AFL season (1968); Forbes gives 1967 as the year purchased. Family stake percentages not stated on any page read. Paycor Stadium capacity, attendance, legal entity, social counts not found on a citable page.
ownership_summary: Owned and run by the Brown family: Mike Brown, son of founder Paul Brown, is president; his daughter Katie Blackburn is executive vice president. Forbes lists Michael Brown as owner, with the team purchased in 1967 for $7.5m. No institutional minority stake is reported.
